items.title: 1Password Hacked, Customer Data and Source Code Stolen in GitHub Account Breach
items.snippet: Popular password management software 1Password on Wednesday disclosed a security incident involving its backend systems that led to the unauthorized access of some customer information, but emphasized that customer password vaults and other secrets were not accessed. "While we took immediate steps to contain the incident, the attacker gained access to some of our backend systems and accessed a
items.summary: Popular password manager 1Password suffered a GitHub account breach resulting in unauthorized access to customer data and source code. Customers and developers using integrated services are affected. Review internal systems and rotate any credentials linked to 1Password integrations.

items.title: North Korea-Linked PolinRider Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread Malware
items.snippet: The threat actors behind the PolinRider campaign have been observed planting a Python loader in GitHub repositories, as evidence emerges that the activity may have started as far back as February 2025. items.summary: North Korea-linked threat actors poisoned over 7,600 GitHub repositories with a Python loader malware hidden in utility packages or conftest.py. Developers using affected repositories should audit their dependencies and check for unauthorized code. Upgrade or remove compromised packages immediately.

items.title: Remus malware steals Gmail messages via fake Google Sheets extension
items.snippet: The Remus infostealer is stealing Gmail messages through a stealthy malicious Chrome extension, a capability the malware operators marketed as a zero-day exploit in Google's email service. [...]
items.summary: The Remus infostealer is stealing Gmail messages using a malicious Chrome extension disguised as a Google Sheets extension. Developers and users should review installed browser extensions and remove unauthorized or suspicious ones. Check your browser extensions and revoke unauthorized access.

items.title: Pun: Format, Lint, and Analyze PHP With One Rust Binary
items.snippet: Pun is a Rust binary in public beta that formats, lints, and analyzes PHP 8.3+ code, installs Composer packages, and reads one pun.toml config file. The post Pun: Format, Lint, and Analyze PHP With One Rust Binary appeared first on Laravel News. Join the Laravel Newsletter to get Laravel articles like this directly in your inbox.
items.summary: Pun is a new Rust binary currently in public beta that formats, lints, and analyzes PHP 8.3+ code, installs Composer packages, and reads a single pun.toml config file. Developers can try it by downloading the public beta binary and setting up a pun.toml config file in their project.

items.title: Fake paid expert interviews impersonate brands to steal Google logins
items.snippet: An ongoing phishing campaign dubbed "GoodGuys" impersonates major brands, including Google, Nvidia, Accenture, and SpaceX, to steal corporate Google and Okta credentials using fake invitations to paid expert interviews and webinars. [...]
items.summary: A phishing campaign named GoodGuys impersonates major brands like Google and Nvidia using fake expert interviews to steal corporate Google and Okta credentials. Developers and staff targeted by these invites should remain vigilant and avoid entering credentials on suspicious sites. Rotate your Okta and Google credentials if you suspect compromise.

items.title: ThreatsDay: 10M NGINX Services at Risk, 250+ Malicious Extensions, AI Server Hijacking + 17 More Stories
items.snippet: A website can look perfectly fine to the person running it. Log out, visit the same page, and things might look different. Something similar is happening with browser extensions, where even the way you find and install one can change what it does. Checking whether software works as expected only tells you so much. Then there’s the question of who gets to use what. Stolen logins are opening
items.summary: Multiple vulnerabilities and risks affect about 10 million NGINX services along with malicious extensions and AI server hijacking. Administrators and developers using NGINX and server infrastructure are affected. Audit your NGINX configurations and review installed extensions for unauthorized changes.
